extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal funds (colleges, universities, K-12 school districts), Title IX coordinators, higher-education administrators, compliance officers, and investigators/adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients must conduct Title IX sexual harassment grievance processes under §106.45, including timelines, evidence inspection, investigative reports, supportive measures, advisor access, procedural protections, and records retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful opportunity to participate
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process aims to ensure that the parties have meaningful opportunities to participate in advancing each party's interests in these high-stakes cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grievance procedures should give both complainants and respondents clear, meaningful opportunities to influence case outcomes, be overseen by impartial, unbiased Title IX personnel who do not prejudge facts, and objectively evaluate inculpatory and exculpatory evidence before determinations regarding responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures offered with or without a formal complaint (§106.44(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must offer supportive measures to a complainant with or without a formal complaint being filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered promptly and supportively upon notice of alleged sexual harassment; they should be determined through an interactive process that takes into account the complainant's wishes and explain the option of filing a formal complaint. Many non-punitive actions (e.g., educational conversations) may be used, and emergency removals remain available under §106.44(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to select an advisor of choice (§106.45(b)(5)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to select an advisor of their choice to advise and accompany them throughout the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must send evidence and investigative reports to parties and to the party's advisor, if any; the regulations decline to place the burden on the party to forward materials to their advisor. Recipients may ask parties to confirm whether they have an advisor before sending materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from retaliation (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71 prohibits retaliation (which includes coercion) against any person for participating or refusing to participate in a Title IX proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must protect parties and witnesses from retaliation and coercion; this protection helps ensure complainants will not be deterred from reporting or seeking supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection and review of evidence — baseline ten-day windows (§106.45(b)(5)(vi) and (vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide parties at least ten days to inspect and review evidence directly related to the allegations, and at least ten days to review and respond to the investigative report prior to a determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use business days, calendar days, school days, or another calculation that fits their operations; they may provide more than ten days; the two ten-day periods together typically prevent concluding a full grievance process in fewer than 20 days. Parties' responses may be considered by decision-makers, and sharing the evidence/report is intended to prevent errors and the appearance of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence sent in electronic format or hard copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must send to each party and the party's advisor, if any, the evidence subject to inspection and review in an electronic format or a hard copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use file-sharing platforms (including those that restrict downloading) and still meet the electronic delivery requirement; recipients should also accommodate parties who cannot access digital copies by sending hard copies or using other privacy-protective practices (e.g., encryption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative report must fairly summarize relevant evidence (§106.45(b)(5)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigative report must fairly summarize all relevant evidence, including inculpatory and exculpatory evidence whether obtained from a party or other source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are not prescribed a full template for reports beyond this core purpose; decision-makers must receive the report at least ten days before a determination and parties must have an opportunity to respond. The report may include recommended findings, but the decision-maker must independently evaluate the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on evidence 'directly related to the allegations' and 'relevant' evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection and review are limited to evidence 'directly related to the allegations' and the investigative report must summarize 'relevant' evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits fishing expeditions and requires investigators to focus on matters relevant to the allegations. The Department will not dilute the direct-relationship requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of privileged and medical/psychological records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are expressly forbidden from using a party's medical, psychological, and similar records without the party's voluntary, written consent and from using information protected by a legally recognized privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators and recipients must obtain written consent before using such records; otherwise they cannot be included or considered as part of the evidence subject to inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on inquiries into prior sexual behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence about a complainant's prior sexual behavior are deemed 'not relevant' except for two limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not permit irrelevant prior sexual history inquiries; only the explicitly allowed exceptions may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement for supervised viewing or special master; parties should receive copies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department believes it is important for the parties to receive a copy of the evidence subject to inspection and review rather than be forced to view evidence only under supervised, restricted conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing copies allows parties and advisors to carefully consider evidence over the ten-day period; the Department declines to require appointment of a special master to oversee evidence exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker independence; single-investigator model prohibited for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision-maker cannot be the same person as the Title IX Coordinator or the investigator and must issue a written determination regarding responsibility after independent evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators may include recommended findings in their report, but the decision-maker has an independent obligation to objectively evaluate relevant evidence and not defer to investigator recommendations; written determinations must include specified elements (e.g., description of procedural steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to consolidate formal complaints (§106.45(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may consolidate formal complaints involving more than one complainant or more than one respondent where the allegations arise out of the same facts or circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consolidated, references to singular 'party' etc. include the plural as applicable, and each individual party retains all rights granted under §106.45 (e.g., each complainant must receive the evidence individually, not just a 'lead complainant').

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' ability to provide additional evidence and responses; rules on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may submit written responses after inspecting evidence and the investigative report; recipients have discretion whether to allow additional evidence following inspection and whether to provide each party's response to the other party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional evidence is allowed and summarized in the investigative report, such additional evidence will not qualify as 'new evidence that was reasonably available at the time the determination regarding responsibility was made' for purposes of an appeal under §106.45(b)(8). Recipients may require parties to submit evidence before the inspection window begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must commit to reasonably prompt timeframes (§106.45(b)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must conclude grievance processes within 'reasonably prompt time frames' to which they commit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department allows recipients flexibility to set timeframes but emphasizes the need to balance promptness with thoroughness and fairness. The prescribed ten-day inspection and ten-day report-review windows are baseline protections and were intended to avoid rushed, error-prone determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients bear the burden of gathering evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden of gathering evidence remains on the recipient rather than the parties to the dispute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are obligated to take reasonable steps to collect and present relevant evidence and to ensure parties have meaningful opportunity to understand the evidence the recipient collects so they can advance their interests to the decision-maker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections and delivery flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may use privacy-protective practices (e.g., encryption) and have flexibility in how they deliver evidence and reports (electronic or hard copy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed references mandating or forbidding specific file-sharing platforms; recipients may choose reasonable technical solutions while ensuring parties receive copies and access consistent with §106.45 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: No extension-mandate for false-statement warnings when sending evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require a statement about false statements to accompany sending evidence to the parties under §106.45(b)(5)(vi); warnings about false statements are addressed in §106.45(b)(2) (written notice of allegations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should include false-statement prohibitions where required by §106.45(b)(2) but are not required to restate them when distributing evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery rights limited compared to litigation or criminal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The §106.45 grievance process does not provide parties with civil/criminal discovery rights such as depositions or subpoena powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grievance process incorporates due process principles appropriate to educational institutions rather than imposing full litigation-style discovery obligations on recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period: seven years (§106.45(b)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must retain records of the grievance process for seven years (revised from the proposed three years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain investigative files, reports, determinations, and related records for the seven-year retention period as required by the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training requirement for investigators on relevance and investigatory conduct (§106.45(b)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must be well-trained in how to conduct an investigation and in issues of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training supports appropriate focus on evidence directly related to allegations, avoiding irrelevant inquiries, and producing investigative reports that fairly summarize relevant evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practices that limit party/advisor access to reports or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices or rules that limit a party's or the party's advisor's access to the investigative report violate §106.45(b)(5)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While platforms that restrict downloading may still fulfill the electronic delivery requirement, recipients must not adopt practices (e.g., claiming the report is institutional property and denying access) that undermine the parties' ability to review evidence and prepare defenses.
